description: An A4 activity book for children who love football: build six clubs from name and badge to kits, stadiums, squads and a dice football season, with a Manager of the Season certificate. 112 pages.
card: Six football clubs to build, start to finish.
lead: For children who love football and dream of running their own club.
for: For children who know every player in the squad
For future managers who’d pick a better team than the real one
For football fans who love to draw and design
hero: The Storymaker’s Football Club Book cover

problem.h: They’ve got big ideas for a football club
p: Children who love football already have opinions about kits, badges and who should be up front. Usually it all ends up on the back of an envelope.
A blank notebook doesn’t tell them where to start, so the club never gets past a name.

approach.h: Fifteen pages, from new name to lifting the cup
p: The book takes young managers through six complete clubs. Each one goes from a brand new name all the way to lifting the cup, fifteen pages at a time.
A club idea waits at the start of every club for anyone who gets stuck. The rest is up to them.

offer.h: A whole football world, made by them
offer.p: Big A4 pages with room to design every detail.
features: Names, badges, kits, stadiums and squads, fifteen pages per club.
Ten lessons on names, badges, kits, stadiums, positions, formations and tactics.
League tables to fill in, and a Manager of the Season certificate at the very end.

note: I made this for the children who are always drawing kits and badges and arguing about the team sheet. Now they get to run the whole club.
The dice football season is my favourite part. Every match is a surprise, and the league table really matters.

points: One paperback book, printed and posted by Amazon.
No subscription and nothing to download. Open it and start.
Amazon handles delivery and returns, just like anything else you buy there.

faq: Roughly six to twelve. Younger children can design the badges and kits, and older ones will enjoy the formations, tactics and the full season.
Yes, one ordinary dice for the football season. Any dice from a board game will do.
Do they need to be good at drawing?
No. Kits, badges and stadiums can be as simple or as detailed as they like.
How is it different from The Storymaker’s Comic Book?
The Comic Book is for telling stories in panels. This one is all about building and managing football clubs.
